name: KMS Key Policy Abuse
description: Every KMS key has a policy that says who may encrypt or decrypt with it. An attacker who can change that policy can add themselves or a role they control. They do not need to steal the key bytes; they just get permission to use it. From there they can read encrypted snapshots, secrets, or databases. Key-policy edits should match a change ticket, and wildcard principals in a key policy are a red flag.
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
